data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra that has raised $11.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the climate and energy sector, including QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and forms the basis of valuation. Using total capital raised ($11.5M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $29M. A peer-median approach is not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability required for meaningful triangulation. Constructing a median across all climate and energy comps would introduce substantial benchmark error.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M (low) to $33M (high), with a median point of $29M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty stemming from the absence of tightly-filtered stage-comparable data. Key risks to valuation include stage-progression assumptions for seed companies in this sector, which may vary significantly based on technology maturity, capital intensity, and market conditions. Investors should supplement this analysis with operational due diligence on product-market fit and competitive positioning within the climate technology landscape.
